title: 1812: La Lime's and Le Mai's houses across the river
items: Two more log houses stand on the north bank west of the Kinzie house in 1812, where Captain Whistler's 1808 plan of the fort draws them: La Lime's, the post interpreter's, and Le Mai's, beside the field the plan gives to Mr. Coursell.
The plan names none of its houses there; Surgeon Cooper names who lived in them. Which house was whose is our reconstruction, and each card says so.
Their size is the plan's drawing; their heights and roofs are reconstructed and listed in Liberties. Neither appears in 1835.
